title: Introduction to Messaging and Event-Driven Architecture
description: Learn how decoupled applications communicate using messages and events instead of direct calls.

data.text: Event-driven architecture is a way of building applications where services communicate by sending and receiving events. Instead of one service calling another directly, services publish events and other services react to them. This makes systems more flexible and easier to scale.

terms.definition: A record that something happened, such as an order being placed.
Data sent between services that may include commands or requests.
The service that sends an event or message.
The service that listens for and reacts to events.
Services that do not depend directly on each other to function.

data.title: Why Go Event-Driven?
data.text: Event-driven systems are easier to maintain because services can change independently. If the inventory service goes down, the order service can still accept orders and process them later.

data.title: Key Differences
items: Messages are usually commands that tell a receiver to do something.
Events are notifications that something already happened.
Messaging often expects a response or acknowledgment.
Events are fire-and-forget - multiple services can react to the same event.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Event-driven architecture lets services communicate without tight coupling.
Events notify listeners that something happened.
Messages carry commands or data between services.
Azure provides three main messaging services: Service Bus, Event Grid, and Event Hubs.
